page: Microsoft Azure FX2ms_v2 is a virtual machine configuration providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core via multithreading on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance implements the x86_64 architecture with instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic acceleration. It features 42.0 GB of system memory, equating to 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by a 260 MB L3 CPU cache. The configuration includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, operating entirely with remote attached storage volumes.

Synthetic and system benchmarks reflect the instance's high clock frequency and low core count. Single-core performance is strong, registering in the top tier for Geekbench single-core tests (2335.0) and demonstrating strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (34.91 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.19 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling, placing multi-core Geekbench (2876.0) and multi-core stress-ng tests in the lower percentiles. Potentially uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 21.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth recorded 14.33 GB/sec, reflecting shared memory bus characteristics.

The primary design tradeoff of the FX2ms_v2 is its extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside high single-thread clock rates. For applications constrained by per-core software licensing costs that simultaneously require large working memory footprints, this profile provides high qualitative resource efficiency. However, workloads requiring massive parallel compute, high uncached memory bandwidth, or high-throughput local disk I/O are bounded by the low thread count and absence of bundled local storage. This profile is appropriate for in-memory caching systems, core-licensed relational database engines, single-threaded ETL transforms, and memory-heavy analytical tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure FX2ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-focused virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 42.0 GB of system memory, yielding an uncommonly high ratio of 21.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying on remote premium storage attachments. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core compute and strong single-threaded compression performance, though multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained by the low core count. This architecture delivers high qualitative cost efficiency for software environments bound by per-core licensing fees where tasks require elevated clock speeds and substantial memory density. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive applications, single-threaded batch processing, and memory-bound databases.
